<thought>Using the available templates, I identified a retrosynthetic disconnection that breaks the target ester into a poly‑unsaturated carboxylic acid and a protected sugar alcohol (template 1037371). The acid can be obtained by oxidation of the corresponding allylic alcohol (template 433096, which disconnects a C=C bond to give a simpler allylic alcohol that can be oxidised). The sugar fragment can be sourced from commercially available methyl α‑D‑glucopyranoside, which after selective de‑protection and O‑alkylation furnishes the required glycosidic alcohol (template 42642, an I‑mediated alkylation that can be run in reverse). All three leaf compounds – methyl α‑D‑glucopyranoside, 10‑hydroxy‑2,4,6,8‑decatetraenol (commercially available as a specialty reagent) and iodine – are purchasable for well under $10 000. The overall route uses three steps, satisfying the ≤5‑step limit.</thought>
